dimensions.assessment: Directly affects students, families, teachers, schools, and local governments by addressing the costs of classroom and school supplies.
dimensions.evidence: arbitrary and chaotic tariffs increase the cost of school supplies for students, families, teachers, schools, and local governments.

dimensions.assessment: Caps duty rates at levels in effect on January 19, 2025, and exempts designated items from subsequent duty increases unless specifically excepted.
dimensions.evidence: no duty described in subsection (b) applies with respect to any item described in subsection (c).

dimensions.assessment: Limits tariff revenues for the federal government by preventing duties on covered items from exceeding January 19, 2025 levels.

Requires the Secretary of Commerce, in coordination with the Secretary of Education, to issue regulations designating classroom items and submit periodic reports to congressional committees, alongside a joint resolution of disapproval procedure.
dimensions.evidence: the item is an item used in an elementary or secondary school classroom, as designated through regulations issued by the Secretary of Commerce

dimensions.assessment: Provides an ongoing limitation on duties beginning on the date of enactment, with periodic reporting requirements every 180 days.
dimensions.evidence: Beginning on the date of the enactment of this Act, no duty described in subsection (b) applies with respect to any item described in subsection (c).

missing_information: Exact aggregate dollar amount of tariff revenue that would be foregone.
The precise list of classroom items that will be designated through future regulations.
importance_detail.rationale: The bill limits certain customs duties on specified school supplies and educational materials, creating broad economic and procedural changes for importers, families, and federal trade agencies.
